title: A reporting cycle grants two people each other's salary, and every check reads it as correct
detail: Platform\Access\DataScope::reaches() refuses a reporting chain that repeats - 'a cycle is a data defect, never a licence to widen scope, so it raises rather than quietly truncating' - and Platform\Organisation\ReportingLine does the same over dated assignment rows. NEITHER CAN FIRE AGAINST THIS PRODUCT'S DATA. The surface hands the platform a chain ONE manager long, because employees.reporting_manager_id is a flat current-valued column, and a one-element chain cannot repeat; employment_assignments, which is properly effective-dated and which ReportingLine walks, has zero rows and nothing writes to it. Platform\Organisation is the most orphaned namespace in the tree - five classes referenced by nothing at all, not even a phase gate. So nobody had ever asked the obvious question: does this tenant's reporting data contain a cycle? IT IS A SECURITY FINDING, NOT A TIDINESS ONE, and that is why it was worth building rather than deferring with the assignment migration. The manager role reaches its direct reports. In a two-person ring each IS the other's direct report, so each can read the other's salary, leave and attendance - and every one of those reads is correctly authorised by the decider, passes the scope sweep, and appears in no audit finding, because nothing is broken. The data is just wrong, which is the kind that survives an audit. A reorganisation typed in over an afternoon produces exactly this, and each row looks perfectly ordinary on its own. tools/reporting-lines.php now walks the real data, bounded by the platform's own MAX_REPORTING_DEPTH rather than 'until it repeats' - an unbounded walk over cyclic data is the very hang the check exists to prevent - and it is in the standing suite as a fatal-skip check, because 'no cycles found' and 'nothing was looked at' are the same line of output. It also reports DANGLING managers separately: a manager id pointing at a deleted row means the person has no manager at all, their leave reaches nobody's queue, and the screen shows a manager because the column has a value in it. Two failures, two different fixes, so they are not collapsed. ONE BUG WORTH RECORDING: the first walk marked a node AFTER stepping past it, so the last member of a ring was never in the path and a two-person cycle was reported as one person managing themselves. A true statement about the wrong number of people - which sends whoever has to fix it to one row instead of two. Proven by ringing two real employments in the database and watching the check go red, then restoring them.

title: A health screen assembled from failures that actually happened
detail: Platform\Operations\HealthCheck is this build's own pattern applied to health: a probe that throws becomes a typed UNKNOWN, unknown counts as FAILING, and the report names it - 'because the alternative is a green dashboard produced by a monitoring system that cannot reach the thing it monitors, which is the worst possible arrangement of those two facts'. Six finished classes reached from nothing but a phase gate. There is now an Installation Health screen behind the settings permission. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH HAVING IS THAT NOTHING ON IT IS IMAGINED. Every probe is a failure this build has actually had: the database account that was created successfully and could not sign in (whose only symptom was a banner saying the product was running on JSON files); the table a migration created that the application could not see, because the account holds table-by-table privileges and information_schema only shows a table to an account with some privilege on it; a schema sitting behind the code; the default credential nobody removed; the password floor lowered to 8 and not put back; a reporting cycle granting two people each other's salary; and a statutory pack whose figures are machinery evidence rather than law. A health screen assembled from plausible failures reports on the wrong things while the real ones keep happening in silence. THE PLATFORM REFUSES A CHECK WITH NO OWNER AND NO REMEDIATION - 'an alert nobody owns, with no stated next step, is a notification that trains people to ignore notifications' - so every row states what was observed, what the threshold was, what to do and whose job it is, and the tests assert all four on every check rather than on one. ONE PROBE WAS WRONG ON THE FIRST RUN and it is the exact failure the class exists to prevent: the statutory check reported OK with '0 statutory head(s) in force', because it asked only whether the pack was synthetic and a pack in force on no date is not synthetic either. Zero and correct read identically - and on that probe it would have told an operator payroll was ready to run when nothing at all would be deducted. Zero heads is now failing, and says that nothing being deducted is not the same as nothing being due.

title: The salary component configuration screen, minus its hard-coded customer
detail: The attached artefact was a working component-configuration grid with three problems, all of the same kind: its 25-component catalogue, its calculation types, its employee status fields and its system values were object literals inside the screen's JavaScript - a business list living in the one file a customer never edits - its Company and Branch dropdowns were one customer's own names typed into the markup, and it saved to window.storage, which is a browser and not a payroll. A customer with a component this list had never heard of needed a release; a second customer got the first customer's branches; and a payslip reprinted for March would have been computed from whatever the grid held today. The catalogue is now config/salary-components.json, kinds and calculations and status fields and system values with the reason for each. The scopes come from this tenant's own branches, teams, designations and people, and a scope with no rows says 'none configured' rather than offering an empty dropdown that reads as a screen which failed to load. The rules are effective-dated rows in salary_component_rules: publishing CLOSES every rule in force on the day before and opens the new set, so April still sees April. WHAT THE VERSION LIST ABOVE IT COULD NOT SAY IS WHO. config/salary-structure.json declares components for a whole tenant and has no way to express 'conveyance is 2,400 in Mumbai and 1,600 everywhere else', which is a sentence nearly every Indian company needs and every one of them works around with a spreadsheet. A rule names a company, branch, team, designation or one person, and the most specific rule wins - specificity being COUNTED from the scopes actually set, never typed, because one fact stored twice is one copy that decides which rule wins while being wrong. The refusals are the feature. Nothing publishes while any row is refused, including the rows that were fine: an unknown component, a calculation with its inputs missing, a percentage that is not an exact decimal (`(float) 'forty'` is 0.0, on a number that multiplies somebody's pay), the same component twice for the same scope, two components both claiming the balance, or a status rule against a column `employees` does not have. A half-published set is neither the old rules nor the new ones. Statutory components are marked as such on the row and the screen says plainly that this build computes none of them and that a rate typed there is the customer's figure, not one the product stands behind.

title: The screen the owner asked for, and the two-year-old bug it walked into
detail: The Salary structure page is now the component configuration grid and nothing else: the effective-dated version list and the JSON publish box are gone at the owner's instruction. What they did is not gone - config/salary-structure.json is still what the payroll run computes from, and versions published earlier are still stored and still audited; there is simply no longer a screen on to them. The grid now carries every column and every condition the artefact had: component, type badge, the five scopes, calculation, calculated column, % value, flat amount, and the three builders - a FORMULA of terms with operators, parentheses, system values (calendar days, working days, # Hours) and custom numbers, with a Max OT hours cap that appears only on Overtime Pay and caps the hours dropdown; a SLAB of from/to/amount ranges on a stated basis; and a STATUS rule against a real employees column. Only one applies per row and the rest lock, and switching calculation CLEARS the fields that no longer apply rather than greying a value that would have been published unseen. SCOPES ARE SUGGESTED, NOT RESTRICTED. A dropdown of the tenant's own branches is right when the tenant has branches; on the owner's own installation - a fresh tenant with no masters - it was a column nobody could fill, so the screen was dead before anybody reached the calculation. It is a text box with the real names offered as you type, and a note saying 'not on file' when a typed value matches nothing, because a misspelt branch is a rule that applies to nobody and looks exactly like one that applies to a branch. THE GRID WAS DRIVEN LIVE IN THE OWNER'S BROWSER, and that is what found the rest. Publishing died on a fatal error: 'Data truncated for column id'. The column named was not the offender - MySQL reports a prepared-insert truncation by the TABLE's ordinal rather than the statement's - so SqlStore now attaches the shape of the row it was writing (column, type, size, never the values) to any refused write. That said it in one line: an `id` of 21 characters in a row that should not have had an id at all. The installation's surface/Trail.php still carried 'id' => Store::id(), a file-store id shipped into a bigint column; the fix had been made here and the file had never reached the machine. Every other file in surface/ matched. A trail entry that fails no longer takes the page down with it: the rules were already written when it happened, and 'nothing was published' would have been the wrong thing to tell somebody.

title: The employee field register — one list, three screens
detail: The Add form was seven inputs written into public/app.php: code, name, department, gross, joined on, bank account, IFSC. A customer who keeps a father's name, a UAN or a biometric device id could not record one without a release, on a table that already had columns for all three. Self-onboarding did not exist and the bulk upload had no sample. config/employee-fields.json is now the register: seven sections and about ninety fields, each naming the REAL column on `employees` it is kept in. Surface\EmployeeFields reads it, asks the LIVE table which of those columns exist, and returns one list - inUse() - that the Add form, the new self-onboarding page and the bulk upload sample are all built from. A field ticked appears in three places; a field unticked disappears from three. IT IS PER TENANT AND IT REUSES THE CUSTOMISATION TABLE. The selection is saved through Customisation::saveRaw under the key employee-fields, so it is versioned, audited and tenant-scoped by the same machinery every other screen change already used - a second table for the same idea is the defect this rebuild exists to remove, and it also means the feature works on an installation that cannot run a migration. A FIELD IS ONLY OFFERED IF THE DATABASE HAS SOMEWHERE TO PUT IT. Law 2 says the application never adds a column, so a declared field with no column - mother's name, grade, cost centre, passport, the education section - is shown greyed with 'needs a column' and refused at save time, rather than accepting a value into nowhere. The check is against the live table, so a migration lights those fields up with no edit to the config. The core fields cannot be turned off: an employment with no code is a row that attendance, leave, payroll and every letter point at by a value nobody entered. Saving replaces the whole selection, because the absence of a tick is the instruction. The upload sample is GENERATED, never a stored file: three rows - the label a person reads, the column the importer matches on, and an example - built from the same list. A shipped template goes stale the first time somebody configures a field, and the person filling it in finds out when their spreadsheet is refused. The employment section says out loud that company, branch, department, team and designation are what a salary component rule is scoped by, so a field left uncaptured there is a scope nobody can be matched on - which is the next piece of work.

title: Nothing greyed out: the register stops telling a customer what they may know
detail: The first cut of the field register greyed out any field `employees` had no column for - about thirty of them, the mother's name among them - and refused to capture them. The reasoning was law 2 (the application never adds a column) and it was sound; the CONCLUSION was wrong. Law 2 says where a value may not go, not what a customer may keep about their own staff. A field with no column is now kept BESIDE the record, in employee_field_values - employment code, field code, value, one row each - which ships with a migration and falls back to the file store until it runs, so it works on an installation that cannot run one. A column is still the better home and is used whenever the table has one; the register says which shelf on every row, so nobody has to guess where a value went. THE DATA TYPE IS THE CUSTOMER'S TOO. Every row carries a dropdown - Text, Numeric, Alpha Numeric, Date, Boolean (Yes/No/NA), List - and what they choose decides the control the Add form and self-onboarding render and the type row in the upload sample. Fields that are lists (gender, blood group, category, marital status, every lookup) start as List. One bug found while wiring it: `$field + ['type' => ...]` kept the catalogue's suggestion and silently discarded the type the customer had chosen - PHP's union operator keeps the LEFT key. array_merge, and a test that saves a type, reads it back through a NEW object and asserts the chosen value rather than the shipped one. The upload sample now carries four rows: the label a person reads, the column or field code the importer matches on, the data type, and an example.

title: Organization Setup, and a payslip format that knows whose payslip it is
detail: The sidebar now separates CONFIGURATION from the screens people work in: an Organization Setup / Configuration section holding Employee fields, Salary structure and the new Payslip format. Setting up the product and running it were the same menu, and a customer could not tell which screens change how the product behaves. PAYSLIP FORMATS, PORTED FROM THE OWNER'S ARTEFACT AND SCOPED THE SAME WAY EVERYTHING ELSE IS. A format names a company, branch, department, designation or one person, and the most specific one wins - the same ladder, counted the same way (from the scopes actually set, never typed), as the salary component rules. That was the point of the instruction 'no ambiguity should be in differentiating these': two configuration screens resolving 'who does this apply to' by two different ladders is how nobody can explain why a payslip looks the way it does. A format naming a branch does not apply in another branch - not a weaker match, not a match - and two formats for exactly the same scope are refused by name at save time. The component list is config/salary-components.json, the same catalogue the salary structure screen configures rules from; a second hard-coded list would let somebody design a payslip around a component payroll does not have. A line can be reordered and RENAMED for the printed slip without detaching it from the component that produced it. IT DECIDES PRESENTATION, NEVER MONEY, and the payslip says so. The payslip screen resolves the format from the employee's own company, branch, department, designation and code, prints the lines in the configured order under their configured names, names the format on the face of the slip, and - when the format hides lines the run computed - says how many are folded away and that they are still in the totals. A payslip that disagrees with the bank transfer is the one document this product must not be able to produce. A format is RETIRED rather than deleted: the store refuses write() on a tenant-scoped collection (it would delete other tenants' rows), which was the right refusal for the wrong reason here - the better answer is that a payslip was printed in that format, and why last March's slip looked the way it did has to survive this March's tidying up.

title: The artefact itself, and the setup fields SmartPRS 2 asks for but does not keep
detail: The payslip designer had been rebuilt in this product's own styling, and it was not what was asked for. The screen is now the ARTEFACT: its markup, its stylesheet, its context bar, its formats rail, its editor, the live payslip on the right, its toast. Three things are not the artefact's, and each is a fact it could not know - the component library is config/salary-components.json rather than a JavaScript object, so a payslip cannot be designed around a component payroll does not have; the company, branch, team and designation lists are this tenant's Organization Setup records rather than one customer's names typed into the file; and a format is saved on the SERVER, per tenant, versioned and audited, rather than in browser storage, which is one person's browser and nobody else's payslip. The seeded demo formats are gone: inventing three formats belonging to a named customer is how demo data reaches production. The stylesheet is scoped to #pf-app, because the artefact's own --bg, --accent and --border would otherwise repaint the whole application. The designer hands back the whole list, so the whole list is reconciled: every format saved, every format no longer in it retired - one the customer removed on screen that quietly stayed in the database would go on printing somebody's payslip. Nothing is written while any format is refused, and two formats sharing a scope are caught within the posted set as well as against what is stored. ORGANIZATION SETUP NOW ASKS FOR WHAT SMARTPRS 2 ASKS FOR - AND KEEPS IT. SmartPRS 2's department form has four inputs; its departments table has two columns. Three of those inputs go nowhere: typed, submitted, dropped. The fields are ported here with the columns to hold them - code, description and an Active/Inactive status on departments, designations and branches; code, legal name and state on companies - and the company form carries the whole branding set the table already had: brand colour, logo, logo text, website, address, type. Two checks caught real things on the way through. The gate found a `(float)` cast on a preview amount: law 7 has no exception for a number that is only being looked at, and the one place a float creeps in is the place nobody thought it mattered. The scope sweep reported the designer refusing to show somebody their own record - because its `?id=` meant a FORMAT while every other screen's means an employment. It is `?format=` now: a false leak of that shape trains people to ignore the check that finds the true ones.

title: Bulk attendance: a spreadsheet becomes punches only when somebody approves it
detail: SmartPRS 2's AttendanceBulkController (rev 82) is ported as surface/AttendanceBulk.php and the attendance-bulk screen: download one of two CSV templates (one row per employee-day, or one row per punch), upload, every row kept with a verdict, the batch approved or rejected as a whole; an approved row becomes ordinary punches in attendance_logs with source=bulk and external_id=bulk:<batch>:<line>:<direction>, so the register settles them like a device's and approving twice writes nothing. Four things SmartPRS 2 does here are refused: matching by name when two employments share it (both codes are named instead), guessing a date format (four are declared; a value must read back as itself), writing punches on upload (upload writes claims; only attendance.bulk.decide writes punches), and deleting a bad row (it is withdrawn and stays, so file and batch agree line for line). Its own table, attendance_bulk_rows, by migration - SmartPRS 2 created attendance_pending at request time inside the controller, which is why the ported attendance_pending is the device queue and has a different shape. Same file-store fallback and banner as the component rules until the migration runs. Both bulk permissions granted to the administrator, a stated ceiling. FOUND ON THE WAY IN: seven test assertions left stale by the float removal at the end of the last session (dashboard, module display, bounded reads expected floats and an unbounded search) - fixed to assert the exact integers and decimal strings the code now returns; and schema_test refuses any column ending in _at that is not DATETIME, which renamed in_at/out_at to in_time/out_time before the first run. 8,222 assertions, 0 failures.

title: Attendance report: the muster, from the register's own settlements
detail: SmartPRS 2's AttendanceReportController is ported as surface/AttendanceReport.php and ?r=attendance-report: every employment in the viewer's scope, every day of a range (at most two months), one cell each - status letter, late marker, manager's rating - with totals, a per-day drill-down (sessions, breaks, unpaired punches, the settlement trace, a 1-10 rating with remarks into the ported attendance_ratings) and a CSV export. Nothing is computed here: a cell is Attendance::settledDays(), the same DaySettlement and published rules the payroll register pays from, so the report cannot disagree with the payslip - SmartPRS 2 pairs punches a second time and judges lateness against a second shift hard-coded in the controller. A day with no punches is a cell, classified by the rules through the new Attendance::dayWithoutPunches() (ABSENT, WEEKLY_OFF, HOLIDAY), or ON_LEAVE from an approved request, or blank when it has not happened; SmartPRS 2 omits such days and GENERATES DEMO PUNCHES into attendance_logs for any day without logs, which is the /app/data fabrication defect in a second place - there is no such branch here. Cell letters are derived from the status name so a status a tenant publishes tomorrow needs no code. attendance.report.view granted to administrator and manager; rating needs a deciding role and the row scope. 60 assertions.

title: Today: the signed-in person's own day, and nobody else's
detail: SmartPRS 2's /app/today panel is ported as ?r=today: first in, last out, worked so far, break, late beyond grace, the sessions, and the last seven days as letters - all from AttendanceReport::day() and muster(), so it is the register's arithmetic. It takes NO id: the employment is Scope::own() and an unbound account is told so. SmartPRS 2 falls back to matching the employee by the user's NAME, which shows one Ravi the other Ravi's punches; there is no such fallback.

title: Absence sweep, report filters, daily rows with chosen columns, and an inbox that shows only yours
detail: SmartPRS 2's AbsenceService (F10) is ported as surface/Absence.php and ?r=absence: sweep a past day over every active employment, skip anybody with a punch or an approved leave, and call a day absent only when the published rules say ABSENT through Attendance::dayWithoutPunches() - a fourth copy of the absence test in SmartPRS 2 is one call here. Who is told (employee, reporting manager) is a versioned customisation declared in config/absence.json; it ships OFF as SmartPRS 2 does. Messages go through Notifications with a dedupe key of employment+date, so the same morning swept twice tells nobody twice; the log is the outbox filtered to the two declared events. THE SWEEP FOUND A LEAK: the inbox showed the whole tenant queue to whoever opened it, so the first message about somebody other than the reader put a colleague's code on a viewer's screen and the scope sweep failed. Notifications::queuedFor() and the inbox now show a person their own messages unless they hold audit.tenant.read. AT THE OWNER'S REQUEST, the attendance report gained company/branch/department/designation/team/employee filters from orgScopes, a Daily rows view in SmartPRS 2's shape (one row per employee-day: code, name, company, department, designation, reporting manager, date, shift, status, first in, last out, total, break, IN, OUT, logs), a Configuration screen (?r=configure-attendance-report) where the tenant chooses which of the sixteen declared columns print - declared in config/attendance-report.json, saved as a versioned customisation - and a day inside an approved leave prints Leave automatically. 22 + 9 new assertions.

title: The sidebar is SmartPRS 2's sidebar
detail: At the owner's request the menu follows SmartPRS 2's sections - Main, Hiring & Onboarding, People, Time & Attendance, Leave, Payroll, Compensation & Claims, Statutory & Compliance, Performance & Rewards, Learning & Knowledge, HR Letters, Field Force, Communication, Reports & Analytics, Administration, Organization Setup / Configuration - 16 sections, 110 items. Every dedicated screen and every one of the 84 module screens now has a place: a menu item may name a `module` and it opens ?r=m&k=… marked with that module's own declared view permission, or a `route` for a dedicated screen. Navigation::forViewer() hands the shell an href so the template stops composing one; Navigation::problems() and navigation_test.php check a module item against modules.json and a route item against the front controller. A locked item is still shown with its lock, so every role sees the same shape of product.

title: Recruitment pipeline, the sidebar as the owner dictates it, and the People sub-menu
detail: surface/Recruitment.php and ?r=recruitment port SmartPRS 2's RecruitmentController: raise a requisition (REQ-yyyy-nnn, pending), approve or reject it with a reason, add candidates against an approved open requisition or into the pool, move them one declared stage at a time (config/recruitment.json holds the stages, sources, interview modes and recommendations that are PHP constants in SmartPRS 2), schedule and record interview rounds, and hire from the offer stage - which creates the employment, opens its leave balances, marks the candidate hired and fills the requisition, closing it when full. hired is never a stage a candidate is moved to, a hire is refused when the code is already an employment and never linked by name, and nothing is deleted. 41 assertions. THE SIDEBAR: the owner will dictate the sub-menus section by section, so the sixteen sections are drawn even when empty (Navigation keep_when_empty, 'Sub-menus to be assigned'). Dictated so far - Hiring & Onboarding: Recruitment, Onboarding Status, Self-Onboarding, Background Verification. People: Directory, Probation, Backed up / Old data (new ?r=archived: archived, exited and inactive employments, kept), Add Employee (alias opening the Directory's form), Import Employees, Teams, Transfers, ID Cards (new ?r=id-cards: a printable card from the record, nothing typed twice), Document Tracker, Exit & FnF. Found: csrf_test reads the literal name="csrf" within 400 bytes of each form, so a token emitted through a variable fails it - forms carry the literal input.

title: Probation board, Email and Image/PDF/Doc field types, Time & Attendance sub-menu, Shifts in setup
detail: surface/Probation.php and ?r=probation port SmartPRS 2's ProbationService: the board of everybody on probation bucketed by the declared milestones (config/probation.json: default months, reminder days - versioned through Customisation), confirm and extend with history in the ported probation_events - and CONFIRMATION IS A TIMELINE EVENT through Surface\Timeline, so payroll and the F&F read the day probation ended from the same record; an empty timeline has its joining recorded from doj first, and the screen says so. The scope sweep caught the history card printing a colleague's code before the row lock - fixed, and the picked employment is now shown with its state so the owner's own record is reachable. EMPLOYEE FIELDS gained the two data types the owner asked for: Email (an email box) and Image/PDF/Doc (a file picker; the file lands under public/uploads/<tenant>/employees/ and the field holds the path - the Photograph ships as one, the emails as Email). The Add form and self-onboarding post multipart; a wrong kind or an oversized file is refused with the field named. SIDEBAR: Time & Attendance dictated (Daily Attendance = the report's daily view, Attendance Report, Manual Entry = the attendance screen, Attendance Correction, Absence Alerts, Biometric Devices, Biometric Device Setup, API Keys, Pending Punches, ZKTeco Devices = the punch import, Geo-Fence Map, Geo-Fence Rules, Working Shifts, Late & Comp-Off Policy) and Shifts added to Organization Setup (setup-shifts alias). Bulk attendance stays reachable at ?r=attendance-bulk but is not in the dictated menu.

title: Import employees: the upload sample, filled in and brought back
detail: surface/EmployeeImport.php and ?r=employee-import port SmartPRS 2's EmployeeImportService onto the ported employee_import_jobs table. The sample the Employee fields register already generates IS the format - the import matches columns by the code row's names, skips the sample's type/allowed/example rows, and checks every cell against the field's declared type (Y-m-d dates, emails, list values, lookups against this tenant's Organization Setup). A row with any problem is refused whole and named by line; the same code twice in a file is refused on the second; an existing code is skipped or updated by the uploader's explicit choice, never duplicated. Preview writes nothing and spools the file under storage/imports/<tenant>/<token>.csv; commit reads that same file back, refuses a second commit, opens leave balances for each new employment, and the job records created/updated/skipped/refused with an errors CSV. 27 assertions. public/uploads added to .gitignore for the new file fields.

title: Attendance correction queue and the ID card PDF
detail: ?r=attendance-corrections is the approver's queue: every regularisation request in the viewer's scope, filtered by state, decided in place - Regularisation::all() joins forEmployment(). ?r=id-cards gained Print ID Card PDF: surface/IdCardPdf.php writes a CR80 PDF by hand (no library - the repository forbids a new dependency without asking) with Helvetica, the tenant's navy and gold, a JPEG photograph embedded via DCTDecode and a PNG honestly shown as 'photo on file'; qpdf --check passes. Names outside Latin-1 are transliterated. 11 assertions.

title: ID Card Format: the card is a format, designed with a live preview
detail: ?r=configure-id-card under Organization Setup, at the owner's request: choose the fields (Emp. ID, name, designation, department, branch, DOJ, DOB, blood group, mobile, email, address, emergency contact, biometric id, PAN, UAN, ESIC, employee signature line, authorised signatory line, valid-till text) and their order, the header (logo, company name, address, photograph, a title such as STAFF), six colours, the footer with {company}, the size (CR80, CR79, CR100, A7, custom mm) and portrait or landscape - with the card redrawn on the right from the form as it is edited. Declared in config/id-card.json, saved through Customisation as a version (surface/IdCardFormat.php). The ID Cards screen and the PDF (IdCardPdf::renderCard) render from the same format through one idCardFor()/idCardHtml() pair, so what is previewed is what prints. Dimensions are tenths of a millimetre and points are computed by integer arithmetic, because the law-7 gate cannot tell a millimetre from a rupee and an allow-list entry is a review for ever. 20 assertions; PDF checked with qpdf and rendered.

title: --help
People → Transfers ported
detail: surface/Transfers: raise (branch/department/company, effective date, reason; one open transfer per employment), decide (maker≠checker; applies at once when due), applyDue, apply writes TRANSFERRED to the timeline and moves the employment row; transfer-order letter template; ?r=transfers list/raise/decide/letter, scoped by the employment moved. 24 tests. Got wrong first: letter placeholders carried their own spacing and the renderer trimmed it — spacing moved into the template.

title: Main tab rebuilt: Live Salary, Escalation Desk, Approvals Inbox, Notifications, AI Assistant, How It Works
detail: Live Salary runs the month-so-far through PayrollPeriod + PayrollRun (payroll.view for others, own row otherwise). Escalation Desk renders Surface\Sla::review() and queues approval.escalated in-app notifications to the role's users linked to an employment, deduped per request-step-approver. Notifications split out of the inbox. AI Assistant is a phrase table (config/assistant.json) in front of the screens' own code — no model, nothing leaves the server. How It Works renders config/how-it-works.json against the live menu. Got wrong first: 'approvals' outscored 'overdue' in phrase length; notice/problem are null before any action.

title: Hiring & Onboarding → Self-Onboarding ported
detail: surface/SelfOnboarding: invite (single / bulk CSV / for an existing employment), token link that opens without an account (?r=onboard&t=, rendered outside the layout), candidate form = EmployeeFields::inUse() minus code/CTC/status/pay basis + documents() as upload slots, save merges, submit refuses with required fields named, HR console verifies per field + email/mobile, correction reopens the link with the note, approve injects through the Add form's own path (code/CTC/DOJ typed by HR, leave balances opened) or updates the existing employment. 46 tests. No OTP: no transport exists, so the token is the credential and HR's tick is the human check. Got wrong first: exposure sweep counted the public page as a screen without its control — excluded by name.

title: Escalation Desk = SmartPRS 2's Escalations register + SLA breaches; Live Salary picker; How It Works card grid
detail: Escalations register (date, company, bank, team, issue, severity, priority, status, action taken) through the module engine with SmartPRS 2's Add Escalation dialog and inline status/action update; module-save learned back=escalation-desk. Live Salary gained the All Employees / one-employee picker with the earnings/deductions breakdown card. How It Works laid out as SmartPRS 2's icon card grid. Found: escalations.bank is a lender name, allow-listed in sensitive_fields_test.

title: Recruitment to SmartPRS 2's screen; global readability styling
detail: Tabs Pipeline/Requisitions/Talent Pool/Hiring Drives/WhatsApp Campaigns, stage chips, six header buttons (Salary Simulator → payroll what-if, Template, Import from Portal, Bulk WhatsApp from file, Raise Requisition, Add Candidate) as dialogs. New surfaces HiringDrives (hiring_drives + hiring_drive_candidates; cancel, never delete) and RecruitCampaigns (recruitment_campaigns/messages; queued only — no WhatsApp provider; export + responses). Recruitment gained template/import/pool; Start self-onboarding from an Offer/Hired candidate creates the invitation. Styling: bold navy/orange headings, lit-up focused and filled fields, 14px base.

title: Organization Setup → Leave Types + Holiday Calendar + leave grants
detail: LeavePolicy and Calendar now carry a Customisation overlay (tenant's own type list replaces the shipped one; holidays + weekly offs overlay the file; shift and proration stay in the file). Holiday Calendar: year picker, date → day auto, type dropdown from config/calendar.json holiday_types; a save touches one year. Leave Types: editable table (paid, opening, accrual, maximum, carry forward, encashable). Grants (LeaveGrants, customisation key leave-grants): type, days, carry-forward Y/N, scope by company/branch/department/designation/team/employee; Apply posts grant:<id>:<year> once per employee per year (from joining date for that year's joiners); year-end Lapse posts LAPSED for non-carry-forward grants. Leave::lapse added. 49 tests. Got wrong first: an unmatched string replace silently left LeavePolicy without saveTypes; a ')' inside a quoted string swallowed a line in Calendar.

title: Payroll sub-menus, Branches setup, any-year pickers, Financial Year
detail: Payroll: Pay Cycle & Lots (config/pay-cycles.json vocabularies; rules as customisation; lots = register runs), Salary Schedules / Deductions Ledger / Payout Reconciliation with SmartPRS 2's fields declared in modules.json (permissions payroll.view/payroll.run), Generate Payroll and Salary Approval as doors into the register, Payslips → batch, Salary & Commission Ledger (payslips + commissions + payments + deductions merged, paise as ints). Branches setup: code/name/city with hints, Edit/Delete per row (soft: deleted_at), Add Branch bottom-left, Save bottom-right; orgScopes skips retired rows. Year pickers accept any year (holidays, financial year). Financial Year: start month + active year as customisation, per-year payroll summary. navigation_test now reads route rewrites.

title: Salary Approval: HR → Finance two-step, as data
detail: config/payroll-approval.json declares the steps (key, label, permission); Register::approve signs the next step, intermediate stage kept in status as <key>_approved, signatures in approval_note; each signer must differ from the closer and every earlier signer; final step approves for payment. Administrator gained payroll.payout.authorise. One step when no config is given, so every existing caller is unchanged.

title: Onboarding Status + Background Verification to SmartPRS 2's screens
detail: Onboarding: config/onboarding.json checklists (New joiner, Transfer) copied onto a board per employment at start; tick/untick; status derived; start one, start for recent joiners, auto-start on self-onboarding injection and on an applied transfer (Transfer list). BGV: config/bgv.json checks/outcomes/statuses; per-check outcome, agency, verified on, re-verify months → next due; overall derived (any flag = discrepancy) with an override kept beside it; due-within-30-days banner; stored compact in the ported VARCHAR(255) checks column. 45 tests.

title: People → Teams, Document Tracker, Exit & FnF to SmartPRS 2's screens
detail: Teams: PRS2 fields (name, function, company, manager, team leader, status) through module-save with an Add/Edit dialog and members counted from employees.team. Document Tracker: grouped by employee, kinds counted, expiry tracked (expired / expiring 30 days banner), Add Document uploads a file against a kind (kinds from Employee fields' documents + free text), per-document status/expiry. Exit & FnF: exit record (last working day, reason from config/exits.json, rehire), clearance checklist from config/exits.json + assets/exit interview, final clearance pending/cleared/withheld; cleared writes exit_date/exit_reason/status=exited on the employment; FnF link to the settlement screen with the last working day.

title: Time & Attendance: PRS2 field declarations + Geo-Fence Map
detail: Working Shifts, Late & Comp-Off Policy, Geo-Fence Rules, Biometric Devices, Pending Punches carry SmartPRS 2's labels, hints and options in config/modules.json (device comm key behind tenant.settings.update). Geo-Fence Map draws every rule and branch point to scale on an SVG grid — no map tiles, no dependency, integer micro-degrees — with an OpenStreetMap link per rule. how-it-works section keys aligned with the menu (time, compensation, statutory, admin).

title: Holiday / W.OFF Schedule: weekly-off patterns
detail: Renamed from Holiday Calendar. Calendar gained weekly_off_nth (weekday → occurrences 1..5), isWeeklyOff(date) used by Attendance and ChargeRules (was two in_array copies), weeklyOffLabel(). Screen: quick patterns (Every Sun; Sat+Sun; Sun + 1st & 4th Sat; 2nd & 4th; 1st/3rd/5th; …) and a Day × (Every, 1st…5th) checkbox grid — any combination.

title: Working Shifts: company from Organization Setup, time pickers, Save
detail: Modules engine: employer_company_id / branch_id / department_id / designation_id / team_id default to a lookup of the Organization Setup table (ORG_LOOKUPS) unless a module declares its own — applies to every module screen; an empty setup list still renders as a dropdown that says where to add rows. Shifts start/end declared type time. Module form button reads Save / Save changes.

title: Module rows: Edit + Delete (retire) on every module list
detail: Modules::retire — deleted_at stamp where the table has one, else a retired value from the status vocabulary, else refused; list hides deleted_at rows and dims inactive ones. modules-writable probe sends nothing for an Organization Setup link whose table is empty.

title: Branches save on a behind-migration DB; lat/lng back; Departments company+branch; standing warnings only on sign-in and Health
detail: branches-save writes only columns the table has and says which are missing (the owner's DB predates migration 001200: no code/is_active). Latitude/longitude fields restored. Departments: Company and Branch pickers (migration 001400 adds departments.branch_id; head via employees lookup). The two standing warnings moved to sign-in + Health.

title: Designations to SmartPRS 2's screen; module header shows count, description, Add button
detail: Migration 001500 adds designations.employer_company_id and grade; fields Designation / Company (Organization Setup list) / Department / Grade-Band / Code / Status. Every module screen now reads '<n> record(s) · description' with an Add <Item> button and Edit/Delete per row.

title: Companies: colour picker + logo upload; module engine gained color and file field types
detail: type: color renders a swatch picker beside the hex box (kept in sync both ways); type: file renders an upload whose stored path is what the column keeps, with the file shown when present. Uploads go through employeeFileValues (same accept list and size cap). Companies declares both.

title: Module list: tolerate declared-but-missing columns; singular labels; duplicate notices removed
detail: A column declared in modules.json that this installation's table lacks prints as — instead of a warning. Add/Edit buttons use a proper singular (Company, Branch). The fifteen screen-local notice/problem prints were duplicating the layout's own; removed.

title: Branches: no double save, company kept
detail: Post→redirect→get after branches-save (a refresh re-posted the form and inserted the id-less row again); a new row whose name or code already exists is refused; the company dropdown compared a string id with an integer array key, so the saved company never showed as selected — cast (same bug in Teams). Flash notice/problem carried across the redirect in the session.

title: Employee fields: Select all + per-section select-all
