(1) "why email IDs are not listed here?" -- most rows showed "not linked" in the Email column, which was reading a LOGIN's email only; an employee with no login yet (most of the tenant) still has an email on file in the Directory, and showing "not linked" in its place read as a missing address rather than a missing login. Fixed: the column now shows the employee's own employees.email for every row (falling back to the login's email only if that somehow differs), with a small "(no login yet)" note only when there truly is no login, and "no email on file" only when the address itself is blank.

(2) "if reset password is clicked, it should give option to enter the new password manually; then at the first time login, the user can change it." No new "must change password at next login" flag or column was added: none existed, and the product already has a self-service change-password screen (My Space, action=change-own-password) that covers exactly this once the owner has told the person their temporary password in person -- ponytail: reuse what already does the job rather than build a forced-change system nobody asked for by name.

`reset-employee-password` now branches on whether a `password` field was posted; php -l clean; committed and byte-verified on device (needed a force:true retry -- see the device_commit_files timing note logged separately).

title: Roles & Permissions' Role list, and every login a Reset Password auto-creates, now come from Organization Configuration -- not a 3-way keyword guess
detail:
Owner, with screenshots of the Roles & Permissions Role dropdown (Administrator / Reporting manager / Employee (viewer) only): "Why Role dropdown is NOT updated yet with the list from Organization configruations? Do this at all relevant places" -- then, after an initial clarifying question, firmly: "It was clearly mentioned n number [of] time[s] ... everything and all the dropdowns should come from the Organization Configuration tab setup" and "why are you manually adding the dropdowns and changing the logic?" Read as a direct instruction rather than asked again: this build already had a `roleOfDesignationText()` keyword heuristic (director/admin/owner/founder/ceo/cxo/head -> administrator; manager/lead/supervisor -> manager; else -> viewer) forcing every Organization -> Role/Designation Setup Role value into one of 3 fixed tiers, documented in roles.php's own comment as a deliberate choice "not silently faked" -- but the owner has now explicitly asked for the real thing, which this build's own architecture turned out to already support almost everywhere:

- `RoleMatrix::save()` already looped over `Authorisation::roles()` generically -- zero changes needed.
- `Users::undeclared()`/`create()`/`setRole()` already validated against `Authorisation::roles()` dynamically -- zero changes needed.
- Payslip Format's and ID Card Format's own Role SCOPE dropdowns already read the real Organization Configuration Role text directly via orgValueOf() -- they were never using the heuristic; already correct.

The actual gap was exactly two spots: Authorisation::__construct() hardcoded 3 role arrays as the whole role universe, and User Management's Reset Password auto-assigned a brand-new login's role by guessing via roleOfDesignationText(). Fixed both. Authorisation::__construct() gained an optional `array $customRoles` parameter (public/app.php passes every distinct, trimmed, non-blank value of orgNames($store)['designation_roles'] -- the exact same source the Payslip/ID Card Role scope already reads); each becomes its own Role::publish()'d entry and its own Assignment, keyed and labelled by its own text, skipped only when it case-insensitively collides with a built-in tier's key or label (so a designation Role literally typed "Administrator" cannot shadow the real one with a second, differently-permissioned entry of the same name). A brand-new custom role starts with NO grants at all -- Law 5, fails closed -- rather than inheriting one of the 3 hand-picked defaults, since there is no sensible built-in default for a role only the owner defined; the owner visits Roles & Permissions once to grant it whatever it needs, through the exact same audited/versioned override every role already saves through. `reach()` was left as-is: its existing `default => 'self'` already covers every custom role correctly and conservatively -- a real per-role reach setting (tenant/team/self) is not built and is called out in the new code comment as follow-up work, not silently guessed at.

User Management's reset-employee-password action now assigns `trim(orgValueOf($store, $target, 'role'))` directly (falling back to 'viewer' only when the designation's own Role field is blank) instead of guessing a tier -- a brand-new login now genuinely gets the role the owner typed for that designation. `roleOfDesignationText()` itself, now zero call sites anywhere, was deleted rather than left as unreachable code with a stale warning comment. roles.php's Designation filter, which used to force-fit every designation into one of 3 buckets via the same heuristic, now does an EXACT match against the selected role's own text -- correct now that a role can genuinely equal a designation's Role field, and for the 3 built-in tiers this will typically show no designations, which is accurate (they are generic access tiers, not job titles anyone types into Role/Designation Setup), not a regression.

Verified with a standalone script (no composer/vendor available in this container) that requires the real Platform\Access classes directly and exercises the edited Authorisation with ReflectionMethod-free direct calls -- 15 assertions: the no-custom-roles case is byte-for-byte the old 3-role behaviour (regression guard), custom roles from Organization Configuration appear as real independently-checkable roles, duplicates and blank entries are deduped/dropped, a role colliding with a built-in tier's name does not shadow or duplicate it, and a brand-new custom role holds no permission at all until granted -- all passing. php -l clean on all three touched files (public/app.php, surface/Authorisation.php, surface/screens/roles.php); committed and byte-verified on device. Not yet visually confirmed live by the owner -- ask him to open Roles & Permissions and pick a Role from Organization Configuration (e.g. whatever he's named a designation's Role) from the dropdown and confirm it now shows as its own, separately-permissioned entry.

title: Roles & Permissions now gives every menu item its own selectable radio row -- shared-permission items stay one synced switch instead of a read-only badge
detail:
Owner, with two screenshots circling rows under People ("Import Employees") and Time & Attendance ("Attendance Report", "Biometric Devices", and others) showing a plain read-only badge instead of View/Edit/Full/No-access radios: "why is this still not giving the selection for each cell in the rows? Update it for each and every module and for each row. This is what was mentioned multiple times and still this is the error."

This was the documented behaviour from the 10 Sep pass: when two or more menu items declare the exact same permission code (employee.create shared by Add Employee/Import Employees; attendance.report.view shared by Daily Attendance/Attendance Report/Attendance Summary; employee.view shared by 50 items; and 12 more codes the same way -- ~148 item-instances across the whole nav tree, mapped in full this pass before touching anything), only the first item got editable radios and every later one rendered a read-only cross-reference badge. The reasoning on record was that two independent radio groups sharing one `name` attribute would 'silently drop whichever one a browser posts last' -- true for two groups meant to hold DIFFERENT values, but not true here: items sharing a code are not two permissions that happen to look alike, they are the exact same permission, so there is only ever one value to post in the first place.

Rejected the alternative that was scoped first (mint a brand-new, distinct permission code for every one of the ~130 customer-facing duplicate items, add each to the catalogue, to config/navigation*.json, to that screen's own gate check, and to every role's default grant array in Authorisation.php): that changes what each screen actually enforces for ~130 items at once, on a codebase with a documented history of the 'declared but unheld' bug -- a permission code that exists in the catalogue but isn't granted to any role silently refuses EVERYONE, administrators included. That is a large, genuinely risky change for a request that is really about the GRID's display, not the product's actual access model: the owner wants to see and use a control on every row, not to make Import Employees independently revokable from Add Employee when nothing in the product currently checks them separately.

Fixed at the grid instead, in surface/screens/roles.php only: every row now always renders the same four radio buttons via $stateColumns(), never the read-only badge branch. Rows sharing a code keep the identical `name="grid[role][code]"` -- the browser enforces mutual exclusion by name across the WHOLE form regardless of which row a radio sits in, so picking a state in any one of the rows instantly updates every other row sharing that code and exactly one value posts on save: correct, not a conflict, because it was only ever one underlying switch. The informational "same permission as X above" note stays under the label, reworded to say picking a state in either row sets both, so the owner still knows why two rows move together. $stateColumns() gained an optional $rowKey parameter folded into each radio's `id` only (never its `name`) so duplicate-code rows don't emit duplicate DOM ids.

Verified with a standalone script re-implementing the id/name-generation logic against the owner's own screenshot scenario (Add Employee + Import Employees sharing employee.create; three items sharing attendance.report.view): asserts every row gets all 4 states (no badge fallback), rows sharing a code share the identical name, no id collisions across the whole grid, and each row's initial checked state matches its own current value -- 5 rows / 20 radios, all passing. php -l clean; committed and byte-verified on device (grep-matched the new comment text and note wording post-commit, not just file size). Not yet visually confirmed live by the owner -- ask him to reopen Roles & Permissions and confirm every row, including the ones his screenshots circled, now shows a selectable set of radios.

title: Roles & Permissions grid fix, corrected — shared-name radios were blanking rows out and breaking the column-select checkbox; every row now has its own control, kept in sync by script
detail:
Owner, with a fresh screenshot after the previous pass: most rows in the grid now showing NO selection at all across all four columns, and "If the checkbox beside the access type is selected, it should select for that entire section under that column" -- reporting that the column header's bulk-select checkbox only actually moved one row, not the whole section.

Root cause, found by tracing actual browser radio-group semantics rather than re-testing the HTML in isolation: the previous pass's fix (every row renders 4 radios, rows sharing a code share the identical `name` so the browser's own exclusivity keeps them in sync) rests on a wrong assumption. A browser only ever keeps ONE radio checked per `name`, period -- not one per name per value. When several rows in the same card share a code (this build has codes shared by up to 50 items), the HTML source marks EACH row's matching state `checked`, but as the page parses, each later same-name `checked` radio silently un-checks the one before it -- so only the very last row for that code in DOM order ends up visibly checked, and every earlier row for that code shows blank across all four columns, not just the shared one. The column-select checkbox's JS did the identical thing live: looping over matching radios and setting .checked = true one at a time, each iteration undoing the previous same-name radio. The earlier pass's standalone test only asserted the right `checked` ATTRIBUTE was emitted per row in the HTML source; it never modelled what the browser actually does with two elements sharing a name at parse/interaction time, which is why it passed while the live behaviour was broken.

Fixed properly in surface/screens/roles.php: every row's 4 radios now get a name UNIQUE TO THAT ROW (`cell[role][md5(code|section|label)]`, never posted directly), so no two rows can ever fight over which one is checked. The one value that actually posts for a code (`grid[role][code]`) is now a single hidden field, rendered once by that code's first (canonical) row ($realGrid) -- never duplicated per row. A small script keeps everything showing one answer: on any row's radio change, it copies the new value into that code's one hidden field and onto every OTHER row sharing the code (inside or outside the current card), so "picking a state here or there sets both" is now actually true instead of colliding. The column header's bulk-select checkbox now goes through the exact same sync routine per row it touches, so it correctly updates the whole section's column AND any duplicate row living in a different section, not just the last row processed.

Verified with a second standalone script modelling the fixed design against the owner's own screenshot scenario (3 rows sharing tenant.settings.view in one card plus a 4th elsewhere; 2 sharing employee.create): asserts every row's radio-group name is unique (the actual bug this time), ids still never collide, exactly one real posted field exists per distinct code (never duplicated), and simulating a change on a duplicate row correctly updates the shared hidden field and is understood to affect every row for that code -- all passing. Also updated the stale doc-comment from the previous pass, which still described the shared-name design as correct. php -l clean; committed and content-verified on device (grepped for the new rm-cell/rm-real/sync() markers, not just a byte-size match -- the device's commit-then-stage flush delay bit again mid-pass on an earlier file this session, so content, not size, is what's trusted here). Not yet visually confirmed live by the owner -- ask him to reopen Roles & Permissions and check that every row (including previously-blank ones) shows its current state again, that a column-header checkbox now moves every row in that section, and that toggling a shared-code row (e.g. Import Employees) visibly updates its twin (Add Employee) too.

title: ID card text truncation fixed (preview + PDF); Visitor entry generalised into owner-configurable Visitor/Client/Guest/... card types with a real visit log
detail:
Owner, with a screenshot of a printed card showing 'Amet...' and 'Modern Pr...' cut off mid-word, plus four numbered asks: (1) stop cutting text off; (2) give Visitor cards a real entry form (Name, Mobile, Phone, Address, Purpose of Visit as a dropdown); (3) let the owner add more card types beyond Visitor (Client, Guest, ...) that work the same way; (4) a 9-position anchor picker (top-left, center, bottom-right, ...) for company name, logo, company address, and each employee field. Items 1-3 built this pass; item 4 deliberately deferred as a separate, larger piece of work (see next).

TRUNCATION (item 1). Three renderers draw an ID card and all three were fixed: the on-screen/print HTML (idCardHtml() in public/app.php), its JS mirror in the ID Card Format Designer's live preview, and the hand-written PDF byte generator (surface/IdCardPdf.php, no PDF library in this project). The HTML renderers used a single nowrap line with text-overflow:ellipsis, which crops mid-word the moment text exceeds one line -- replaced with -webkit-line-clamp:2 (supported by every browser this app targets), so company name and tagline wrap to a second line before anything is cut, and the outer card wrapper was changed from a fixed height+overflow:hidden to min-height with no clipping so a 2-line header doesn't overlap the rows beneath it (caught via a Playwright screenshot before committing -- the first version of this fix silently overlapped the footer). The PDF has no font-metrics table, so a small 4-bucket character-width heuristic was added (surface/IdCardPdf.php: charWeight()/textWidth(), explicitly commented as a heuristic, not a real AFM table) to give it textWidth(), fitOneLine() (trim + ellipsis) and wrapLines() (greedy word-wrap, ellipsized final line on overflow); renderCard() now wraps the company name BEFORE the header band is drawn (the band grows 10pt if 2 lines are needed) and fit-checks every other text draw -- tagline, name, designation, field labels and values, footer -- against its real available width instead of drawing it unconditionally. Verified with a standalone script asserting every draw origin stays inside the card's own MediaBox, plus a rendered PDF rasterised to PNG and inspected directly.

VISITOR/CLIENT/GUEST (items 2-3). A Visitor card used to be one hardcoded sentinel with no real data behind it. Generalised: IdCardFormat::EXT_PREFIX marks any owner-added type id alongside the existing VISITOR_ID, one isTemplateId() check and one templateRowFor(id, label) factory replace the old hardcoded visitorRow() (kept as a one-line delegate for compatibility). Card TYPES themselves (Client, Guest, ...) and VISIT PURPOSES (Interview, Maintenance, ...) are both owner-editable lists, built on a new small reusable class, surface/NamedList.php -- an {id, label} list versioned through the same Customisation config store IdCardFormat's own named entries already use, with a stable slug minted once from the label so a later rename never repoints a format or a past visit-log row that already stored the old id. Two new Organization Setup screens (Card Types, Visit Purposes) edit these lists, deliberately reusing the already-granted tenant.settings.view/update permission codes rather than minting new ones, to avoid any risk of the 'declared but unheld permission' lockout pattern this build has hit before.

Actual check-in DATA (name, mobile, phone, address, purpose) is real per-transaction history, not configuration, so it does NOT go through Customisation (which would mean rewriting the whole growing history as one payload on every single visit) -- it goes into a real new table, database/migrations/2026_09_11_000100_create_visitor_log.php (visitor_log: type_id, type_label, name, mobile, phone, address, purpose, created_by, timestamps). This needs the migration APPLYING to the live database before entries can actually be saved -- something the owner does not run himself per this project's standing rule, so until whoever runs composer db:migrate applies it, every code path that touches visitor_log is wrapped in try/catch and degrades to a clear message rather than erroring. The ID Cards screen gained a 'New visitor / client / guest entry' form (Purpose of Visit as a real dropdown sourced from the Visit Purposes list) and a picker over the last 20 recent entries to print a card for; the Format Designer's employee-scope picker and its live preview, and the PDF's photo-box label, all now show whichever type's own label applies (Visitor, Client, Guest, ...) instead of a hardcoded 'VISITOR' string, via one no_photo_label string key threaded through idCardFor()/idCardHtml()/the JS mirror/IdCardPdf::renderCard() (replacing the old is_visitor bool).
next: Item 4 (9-position anchor picker for company name/logo/company address/each employee field) deliberately not built this pass -- a hand-rolled coordinate layout system across the PDF and both HTML renderers is a meaningfully larger, higher-regression-risk piece of work, and this pass already touched the same shared renderers three times over for the truncation fix. Recommend as the next distinct piece of work, once this pass is visually confirmed live. Also: apply database/migrations/2026_09_11_000100_create_visitor_log.php so visitor-log entries can actually save (visitor/client/guest card printing itself works today, it just can't remember a check-in yet). Same two long-standing items as before, still untouched: ID Card Format's Applies-to dropdown truncation (screenshot asked for twice), and per-role REACH setting.
checks: php -l clean on public/app.php, surface/IdCardPdf.php, surface/IdCardFormat.php, surface/NamedList.php, and the new migration. config/id-card.json and config/navigation.json validated as parseable JSON. A standalone script rendering the owner's exact truncation scenario through IdCardPdf, asserting every Td draw origin stays within the card's own MediaBox (pdftoppm-rasterised and visually inspected too). A Playwright-rendered screenshot of idCardHtml() at 500x500, caught and fixed a self-introduced header/footer overlap before it reached the device. A from-scratch standalone script against a fake in-memory RowStore: NamedList save()/all()/label() round-trip including slug stability across a rename; IdCardFormat::isTemplateId()/templateRowFor() for both the built-in Visitor id and an owner-added EXT_PREFIX id; confirmed grep-clean that IdCardPdf.php no longer references the retired is_visitor key anywhere and instead reads no_photo_label; IdCardPdf::renderCard() exercised with a label, a blank label (real employee fallback), and a too-long label, none throwing -- 22 assertions, all passing. device_commit_files for all 7 touched files, then content-grepped (not just byte-size) after the standard wait to confirm the real content landed, not a stale flush.

title: Card Types/Visit Purposes folded into ID Card Format page; back-of-card text; photo shape/border/crop; basic barcode; auto-expiry
detail:
Owner sent a 7-item follow-up plus two rounds of clarifying answers: (1) fold the standalone Card Types and Visit Purposes screens into the ID Card Format Designer page itself; (2) other setup -- per-branch/company designs, QR/barcode, expiry rules, 40 template designs to include with colour customisation; (3) drag-and-drop placement of card elements; (4) customisable photo shape (square/rounded/oval/circle); (5) customisable photo border (single/double/side-opacity-blur, with an adjustable amount); (6) optional back-of-card text with 4-5 pre-drafted, editable samples; (7) photo cropping on upload. Follow-up answers: for item 2, the owner wants per-branch designs, a basic QR/barcode with only basic employee details, expiry rules, and the 40 templates (owner said they'd send files); for delivery, 'all at once' rather than phased.

ITEM 1 (types/purposes into the format page). The standalone id-card-types and visit-purposes routes and nav entries were removed; a new closure ($icNlSection) renders the same NamedList add/rename/remove UI inline inside configure-id-card, once for Card Types and once for Visit Purposes, sharing one small inline script instead of two near-duplicate pages. Nav entries removed from config/navigation.json; save-action redirects updated to land back on configure-id-card.

ITEM 2 (other customisation). Per-branch/company designs: already fully covered by the existing 'Applies to' named-format scoping (IdCardFormat::formatFor()) used by both the PDF print action and the on-screen ID Cards screen -- no new code needed, just confirmed it. QR/barcode: a basic QR code was considered and dropped -- correct Reed-Solomon + matrix placement can't be hand-verified against a real scanner in this environment, and a QR that LOOKS right but doesn't scan is worse than no code. Built Code 128 Subset B instead (surface/Barcode.php, dependency-free, per house rule): a 103-row width table, Start B/Stop patterns, mod-103 checksum, output as a plain module-bit string any renderer draws as bars. Verified structurally (uniqueness/digit-range/sum-to-11 across all 103 rows) and via independent round-trip self-decoding across 9 test strings, since OpenCV's 1D barcode detector proved non-functional in this sandbox even after a QR-based control experiment confirmed the *methodology* was sound -- flagged in code comments as a known verification limit; a real-world scan test is still recommended. Wired in as a new 'barcode' field kind (config/id-card.json), following the same kind-based pattern signature/text fields already used, in the format cleaner, both HTML renderers, and IdCardPdf. Expiry rules: new valid_till_mode (text/days) + valid_till_days on the format; 'days' mode computes issue-date + N days at render time in idCardFor(), overriding any stale static text. 40 templates: NOT built this pass -- the owner sent one low-resolution contact-sheet image of a commercial-looking stock badge pack, not individual files; cloning it 1:1 was declined for both copyright risk and because a hand-written PDF renderer with no vector-import can't reliably re-trace bezier art off a thumbnail grid. Still waiting on the owner's actual files (or confirmation to proceed with an original shape-family x colour-palette system instead).

ITEMS 4/5/7 (photo shape, border, crop). photo_shapes (square/rounded/oval/circle) and photo_borders (single/double/blur, with a 0-100 blur amount) added as config/id-card.json declared lists, validated the same way sizes/orientations already are. All three renderers updated: CSS border-radius for the HTML/JS versions (oval = non-square box at 50%, circle = forced square first); IdCardPdf.php gained shapePath()/roundedRectPath()/ellipsePath() using the standard 4-Bezier kappa~=0.5523 circle approximation (raw PDF content streams have no native ellipse or rounded-rect operator) and uses <path> W n to clip the embedded photo before drawing it; blur border approximated as concentric fading rings in the PDF and an inset box-shadow in CSS (no true alpha compositing in the hand-written PDF writer -- ponytail-flagged). Cropping: a small dependency-free canvas cropper (drag a rectangle over the picked image, crop to a <canvas>, re-encode via toBlob, swap into the file input via the DataTransfer API) wired onto all four photo upload points in the app (employee photo field, the quick-attach ID Cards form, and the account settings photo). Verified end-to-end with a full Playwright simulation (pick file -> overlay opens -> drag -> Apply -> input's File object confirmably replaced with the cropped image).

ITEM 6 (back of card). New back_text field on the format (600-char cap) plus IdCardFormat::backSideSamples(), five pre-drafted, fully-editable paragraphs ({company} property/return, terms of use, emergency/verification, authorisation, code of conduct) offered as a dropdown that fills the textarea, which the owner can then edit freely. IdCardPdf.php generalised from a hardcoded single-page writer to N pages (dynamic object numbering, a $pageNums list, /Pages Kids/Count filled in only after every page is built) so a populated back_text renders as a genuine second PDF page; the on-screen/print HTML renders it as a second card face beneath the front.

ITEMS 3 and 8-remainder NOT started this pass: drag-and-drop placement of card elements (item 3) was assessed as the largest, highest-regression-risk piece of this whole request -- it would mean rebuilding the card layout from flexbox to absolute/anchored positioning across all three renderers (HTML, its JS mirror, and the hand-written PDF), with real risk to the truncation fixes from the previous pass. Deliberately not attempted this pass; flagged to the owner as a separate follow-up, same as the position-picker item was deferred last pass.

Verification: php -l on all six touched files; config/id-card.json and config/navigation.json re-validated as parseable JSON; a combined integration test (long wrapping company name, rounded+double-bordered photo with a real embedded gradient JPEG, barcode with caption, back-of-card text) rendered through both the PDF path (pdftoppm-rasterised, visually inspected) and the HTML/JS path (Playwright screenshot, visually inspected) with no overlap, truncation or rendering defects on either face. device_commit_files for all six touched files, then content-grepped after the standard wait (including confirming the retired id-card-types nav entry is now absent) to confirm the real edits landed, not a stale flush.

title: ID card template gallery: 10 named templates (5 header shapes x colour), a 'Start from a template' picker, header_style in all 3 renderers
detail:
Owner sent an image of a commercial-looking ID badge template contact sheet (~20 thumbnails, diagonal/wave/circular-badge/side-stripe/solid header styles over varied colours) with 'use this image and create templates and have dropdowns to select the template and give names to each template for reference'. Deliberately did NOT trace the specific artwork 1:1 -- both copyright risk (this reads as a purchased stock asset pack) and technical fit (the hand-written PDF writer has no vector-import) argued against it, same reasoning as the earlier 40-template ask. Instead built an ORIGINAL template system in the same genre: 5 header SILHOUETTES (solid band -- unchanged from before; diagonal cut; arc/wave; side stripe; circular badge ring behind the photo) that any of the 6 existing colours can be applied to, plus 10 named starting points (Classic Navy, Diagonal Amber, Diagonal Crimson, Side Stripe Emerald, Side Stripe Purple, Circular Badge Blue, Circular Badge Teal, Arc Sunrise, Arc Ocean, Minimal Charcoal) that a 'Start from a template' dropdown on the Format Designer page fills in (header style, photo shape/border, all 6 colours) -- client-side only, no page reload, and every field it fills stays exactly as editable afterward as the owner asked ('option to modify the colours after selecting the template').

header_style joins photo_shape/photo_border as a config/id-card.json declared list (5 entries), validated in IdCardFormat::clean() the same way. The 4 new shapes are drawn with NOTHING but existing techniques: CSS clip-path (diagonal, arc) and box-shadow (the badge ring) in the HTML preview and its JS mirror; hand-written PDF paths in a new IdCardPdf::headerBandOp()/archPath() pair (diagonal and stripe are straight-line polygons; arc is a single cubic bezier dip across the header's bottom edge, the same kappa-based bezier technique already used for the photo shapes; the badge ring reuses the existing ellipsePath() helper, drawn behind the photo box before it paints over the middle). 'stripe' and 'badge' have no coloured header band at all -- header text switches from header/header_text to text/background, and stripe/badge both had to shift the header text, photo box and footer's left margin so nothing prints under the stripe (caught by an early PDF render: v1 had the stripe drawn OVER the footer text) or under a bad diagonal cut (v1 cut the LEFT side of the header, clipping the owner's actual company name/tagline -- flipped to cut the right side, protecting the text, and moved the small 'title' badge from the band's bottom edge to its top so a white-text-on-cut-away-background invisibility bug on the diagonal/arc styles couldn't happen).

Verification: php -l on all 4 touched files, config/id-card.json re-validated as parseable and counted (10 templates, 5 header styles). All 5 header styles rendered standalone through the real PDF path (pdftoppm-rasterised, a 5-up grid visually inspected -- caught and fixed the diagonal-cut and stripe-overlap bugs above before this passed) and through the real idCardHtml()/JS-mirror path (Playwright screenshot, visually confirmed all 5 match the PDF's shapes). The 'Start from a template' picker's own JS (extracted into an isolated test harness -- a bare form with the same field names plus the exact markup/script block from public/app.php) was Playwright-tested selecting 'badge-blue' and confirmed header_style, photo_shape, photo_border and all 6 colour inputs landed with the template's exact values. device_commit_files for all 4 touched files, then content-grepped after the standard wait (ic-template markup, IdCardPdf::headerBandOp(), IdCardFormat's header_style validation line, and the config's template/header_style counts) to confirm the real edits landed.

title: Administrator self-approval override: the company admin may now approve/decide anything pending for the tenant -- payroll, leave, finance -- even a run or request it raised or closed itself
detail: Owner's instruction, verbatim: "The company admin can approve self or any pending approval whether it is related to Payroll, Finance, Leaves, anything for the entire company. Even if the company admin has generated payroll, the admin can approve it." Two separate live engines carry the "the person who raised/closed this cannot also decide it" control: Register::approve() for payroll runs (config/payroll-approval.json), and Requests::decide() for the generic Leave/Finance/other workflow chains (config/workflows.json) -- a third, more sophisticated declarative engine at src/Platform/Workflow/ already ships a designed-but-unwired SELF_APPROVAL_OVERRIDES mechanism plus a hard Section 56 refusal gate, but nothing currently wires it to a live screen, so it was left untouched. Ruled out adding a new permission code (access.approval.override_self or similar): src/Platform/Access/catalogue.php is headed "GENERATED, DO NOT HAND-EDIT" -- generated from docs/registers/REGISTER-PERMISSIONS.md, itself generated from the blueprint parts, and this session has no access to that generation pipeline. Also confirmed the spec itself already anticipates exactly this: docs/22-PART-XXII, decisions D-XXII-03/D-XXII-04, treat an administrator holding payroll approval and a disable-able two-person rule as deliberate, owner-level, audited configuration choices, not violations of segregation of duties. Implemented instead as a single new role-keyed fact, Authorisation::maySelfApprove(string $role): bool, added right after the existing reach() method whose same shape it copies -- Authorisation.php's own docblock states there is no inline $user['role'] === 'administrator' check anywhere in the surface, and reach() is the one sanctioned precedent for a centralized role-keyed check instead of scattering one. maySelfApprove() returns true only for 'administrator'. Register::approve() and Requests::decide() each gained a trailing $selfApprovalAllowed = false parameter, resolved by the caller from the acting user's role and never guessed at inside the engine class (both classes stay authorisation-blind, same as every other engine in surface/); the existing refusal checks ("the person who closed a run cannot approve it", "you raised this request, so you cannot decide it") now read `if (!$selfApprovalAllowed && ...)`. Wired at the three call sites in public/app.php that call these methods (the approve-period route, the bulk salary-approval loop, and the generic request-decision route), each passing $access->maySelfApprove((string) $session->user()['role']). Left Register::approve()'s separate "already signed an earlier step" check (self::signers()) untouched -- a different rule (no one signs the same run twice across multiple steps), not the self-approval-of-what-you-raised rule the owner asked about, and currently moot since the live config has only one approval step. Verified with a standalone smoke test constructing the real Authorisation, Register, Requests, Store, Structure, PayrollPeriod, Attendance and Leave classes (no mocks): administrator self-approves both a closed payroll run and a raised leave request only when the flag is set; every other role (manager, viewer, an unrecognised role) stays refused with or without the flag; a different person's approval of someone else's run/request is unaffected either way. php -l clean on all four touched files (Authorisation.php, Register.php, Requests.php, public/app.php); device_commit_files then re-staged and byte-compared, matching exactly on the first attempt for all four files.

title: Salary structure screen: "Save all rules" was silently losing every attempt to a stale CSRF token with no redirect to recover from it -- fixed with POST->REDIRECT->GET (the same pattern the branches screen already uses); Slab rows now self-test-compile at save time, same as Manual
detail: Owner reported three symptoms on the Salary structure (Component Rules) screen: a Slab row "not saving" with a "continue without saving" prompt on refresh even though the page said it was saved; the saved calculations not showing up anywhere in Payroll/Payslips; and every generated payslip showing an identical flat 200 deduction regardless of employee. Investigated by reading storage/salary_component_rules.json directly on the device rather than guessing: it had not been touched since 2026-09-08 and held exactly one old rule (a pre-N-branch OT formula) -- nothing the owner configured this week (House Rent, Basic, the Provident slab, the Provident flat) had ever actually reached storage, despite the screen reporting success. Traced the wiring end to end first to rule out "not connected": ComponentRules::resolveFor()/merge()/asEngineComponents() ARE called from Register.php's own run-generation code (not dead code), so the screen genuinely does drive real payroll once a rule is actually published -- the reported "not wired" symptom is fully explained by nothing having been saved in the first place. The flat 200 Professional Tax deduction on every payslip is config/salary-structure.json's own fallback flat structure (ComponentRules::merge() falls back to it for any component no published rule overrides), which is exactly what runs when Component Rules has nothing relevant published. Root cause of the save itself: app.php's CSRF check (Session::verify()) refuses a form whose token no longer matches the session's current one -- a real, working check, not a bug -- but publish-structure and publish-component-rules were the only two state-changing routes in the file that skipped the POST -> REDIRECT -> GET pattern every other save route already uses (the branches screen's own comment names the exact failure mode: "F5 re-sent the form and a row with no id was inserted a second time"). Without the redirect, a save attempt after the token had gone stale (plausible on this screen specifically -- a Slab row alone is four sub-fields per range, so it is filled in over several minutes) left the browser sitting on a POST-result page: refreshing to check re-triggers the browser's own "Confirm Form Resubmission" prompt, and clicking through it just resends the same stale token, refused again -- which reads as "it said saved, then refreshing loses it" from the outside, even though the CSRF refusal's own message already says plainly "nothing was changed... the work is not lost, it simply was not applied." Fixed by adding the same flash-message + redirect pattern the branches screen already established to both routes: every save now lands on a freshly rendered GET carrying the CURRENT token, so a refresh is always safe and a save attempted after the token went stale fails once, visibly, rather than trapping the browser on an unsendable page. Separately, and found while re-reading refusals() end to end: MANUAL calculation rows have self-tested their own compiled expression at publish time since this build got N-branch support (11-12 Sep), but SLAB rows never got the same treatment -- refusals() only checked "is the slab array non-empty", so a slab basis this build cannot map ('CTC'/'BASIC' only) or a malformed range would publish cleanly and only be discovered when a real payroll close tried to build the component. Closed that gap by having refusals() run the same SLAB row through mapSlab() (the real compiler, via a real SalaryComponent construction, which is also what catches overlapping ranges) and report any refusal by row number, mirroring MANUAL's own pattern exactly.

title: Attendance report: two-month muster width cap is a deliberate, reasoned design limit (left alone) -- but a refused date range was also showing a false "no employee in your scope" message underneath the real refusal reason; fixed to show only the true cause
detail: Owner reported the Attendance Report (muster) screen refuses a Custom-dates range from 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-15 with a red banner ("A muster is at most two months wide...") and, separately, shows "0 employee(s) -- No employee is in your scope for this report" even with every scope filter (Company/Branch/Department/Designation/Role/Team/Employee) left at ALL, asking why it would not just show the report. Read AttendanceReport.php end to end: the two-month ceiling is AttendanceReport::dates() deliberately throwing when a range exceeds 62 days, and the class doc-comment already reasons about exactly why -- every employee is fully re-settled from raw punches for the whole range on every request (a ponytail comment on the class names the ceiling plainly: fine for one tenant on a laptop, not for a year across a thousand people, and names the real fix as a punchesBetween() on the store, not a bigger number here). A Jan-Sep span is about 257 days, nowhere near 62, so both the on-screen grid and the CSV export refuse it -- CSV export calls the exact same muster() without lifting the cap, and the wider escape hatch already built for this (musterWide(), "folds days to counts, never draws cells") is not wired into any screen yet. This is a deliberate, reasoned design limit, not a bug, and was left alone. The "0 employees / no employee in your scope" message, though, was a real defect: storage/employees.json was checked directly on the device and this tenant is not empty (one real employee, MD Gulab, joined 2026-09-07) -- the 0-employee result was not a scope problem at all. app.php initialises  to an empty rows array BEFORE the try block that calls muster(); when the range-too-wide exception fires, that catch block sets  and leaves  at its empty default, but the empty-state text underneath never checked whether a problem was already being shown above it -- so a refused range and a genuine empty scope produced the identical, wrong-in-the-first-case message. Fixed by gating that note on  === '''': a refused range now shows only the one true reason (the red banner), not a second, false one under it.

title: KRAs and KPIs (Organization Setup) and KPI Achievements (Performance & Rewards) — collections-industry KRA/KPI catalogue seeded from the owner's own matrix, company/branch/role-scoped targets, and an achievement ledger that computes % Achieved exactly against the target it froze at record time
detail: Owner attached a 175-row “Collection_Recovery_KRA_KPI_Matrix.xlsx” (21 KRAs: Collection/Recovery, Delinquency Management, Bucket Management, PTP Management, Customer Contact, Field Collection, Agent Productivity, Digital Collection, Recovery Quality, Portfolio Quality, Cost Efficiency, Customer Service, Compliance, Data Quality, Team Management, Agency/Vendor, Fraud/Risk, Attendance/Discipline, Workforce Utilization, SLA/TAT, Management) and asked for two things: (1) a new “KRAs and KPIs” tab under Organization Configuration Setup listing the whole matrix with Company/Branch/Role filters to say who a target applies to, and a target box per KPI; (2) a new “KPI Achievements” tab under Performance & Rewards to enter Employee ID/Name, a Date range or Month, a KPI dropdown and an Achieved value, wired to the KPI's target so % Achieved computes accurately in the next column. THE CATALOGUE IS PURE DATA (law 1): the whole matrix (kra, kpi, description, formula) went into new config/kra-kpi.json, each row keyed by a stable slug code derived once from its KRA+KPI names (collection-recovery--collection-amount, etc) so a target or achievement published against it never orphans if the display label is edited later; all 175 codes confirmed unique. TARGETS ARE TENANT DATA, SCOPED AND EFFECTIVE-DATED, on the SAME LADDER AND CONVENTION as salary_component_rules and Pay Cycle's own rules (company/branch/role here, narrower than the full ladder on purpose — the owner asked for company/branch/role, not a per-employee exception): a new class surface/KraKpi.php and a new migration (2026_09_16_000100_create_kra_kpi_tables.php, two tables: kra_kpi_targets, kra_kpi_achievements) ship with this release; the application cannot create them (law 2, no DDL on its own DB account), so KraKpi falls back to the same tenant-scoped JSON file store every other not-yet-migrated feature in this codebase falls back to, with the same on-screen amber banner naming it. Publishing a scope's targets is never an edit in place (law 3): it closes whatever was open for that EXACT (kpi_code, company, branch, role) tuple the day before and opens a new row — only the KPI codes actually submitted are touched, every other scope's rows and every other KPI's rows are left alone, and specificity (how many of the three scope columns are set) is derived, never typed, exactly like ComponentRules::publish(). Blank or the literal word 'All' both mean "any", the same convention ComponentRules/PayCycles already use. Resolution (KraKpi::resolveTarget()) takes the employee's own company/branch/role as NAMES supplied by the caller (public/app.php's own orgValueOf(), already used by every other scoped screen) rather than re-deriving them, so there is no second lookup to drift from that one; most-specific match wins. ACHIEVEMENTS ARE AN APPEND-ONLY LEDGER, exactly like points_ledger: recording the same employee/KPI/period again adds a new row rather than editing the old one, so a correction stays visible as a correction. Every entry FREEZES the target it was measured against (law 4, every number explains itself) at the moment it is recorded — target_value, percent_achieved and a working string naming the exact division and which scope the target came from are all stored on the row, so a target revised in October never silently rewrites what September's percentage meant. % Achieved is computed with Platform\Support\Rational (the same exact-fraction class Assessments::score()/passed() use for test pass rates) — achieved ÷ target × 100, never a float — and refused rather than guessed when no target covers the employee, or when the resolved target is zero. SCREENS: KRAs and KPIs (route kra-kpi, config/navigation.json under 'setup', permission tenant.settings.view/tenant.settings.update matching the sibling Attendance Report Columns screen) — a Company/Branch/Role scope picker (GET) loads that exact scope's currently-open targets into a form grouped by KRA as 21 collapsible <details> sections (the same convention as the ID Card 'Applies to' grid and Holiday scoping), each KPI row showing its description and formula read-only plus one target box; saving publishes only the boxes actually filled in; every target ever published is listed below, newest first, closed rows dimmed. KPI Achievements (route kpi-achievements, under 'performance', permission employee.view/employee.update — no dedicated performance/kpi permission code exists yet in Authorisation.php, and per the 12 Sep precedent (administrator self-approval entry) this session mints no new one, since the catalogue is machine-generated from the blueprint and this session cannot run that pipeline) — Employee ID (with a datalist of active codes), a KPI dropdown grouped by KRA (optgroups), a Month-or-date-range period picker, and an Achieved value; the employee's Name/Company/Branch/Role are read from the Directory by ID, never typed on the form, so they cannot drift from the real record; every recorded entry is listed below with Target, Achieved and % Achieved. surface/Performance.php and surface/Points.php (built in an earlier session, never wired to any route or nav item — confirmed by grep, zero references anywhere in public/app.php) were left exactly as they are; this is a new, separate KRA/KPI feature, not a continuation of those, and both remain available for whenever the owner dictates that section of Performance & Rewards.
correction_to_prior_entry: No — a new, additive feature (Organization Setup and Performance & Rewards each gained one screen); nothing prior was touched.
next: Live click-through still needed (this session has no owner-credentialed browser pass): publish a tenant-wide target, then a branch-scoped one for the same KPI, and confirm an employee in that branch gets the branch figure while everyone else gets the tenant-wide one; record an achievement and confirm % Achieved matches hand arithmetic; try a KPI with no target configured and confirm it is refused by name rather than silently accepted. The Performance & Rewards section still has Performance.php and Points.php sitting unwired — worth asking the owner whether Performance Reviews / Points & Leaderboard should be the next sub-menus built there. kra_kpi_targets/kra_kpi_achievements need the same migrate + grant-application-account.php --apply pair as every other not-yet-migrated table before they leave the file-store fallback — raise with Shashank, never hand the owner the command directly.
checks: php -l clean on public/app.php, surface/KraKpi.php, the new migration, and the new test. A standalone smoke test (tests/kra_kpi_test.php, 29 assertions, run directly against the real classes with the tests/lib/bootstrap.php autoloader in this cloud session — this project has no device_bash, so `composer check` could not be run on the owner's machine from here) covers: the catalogue carries the real 175-row matrix; a KPI code outside it is refused; a non-numeric target is refused; one bad row in a batch blocks the whole publish (never a partial one); a branch-scoped target outranks a tenant-wide one for an employee in that branch while everyone else still gets the tenant-wide figure; re-publishing the same scope closes the old row rather than editing it, and a date before the revision still resolves the old target (a September achievement stays explained by September's number); an unconfigured KPI resolves to no target rather than a guess; a recorded achievement freezes its target and computes an exact percentage (1,530,000 of 1,800,000 = 85, not a rounded approximation); recording the same employee/KPI/period twice keeps both rows; and 'All' on publish reads identically to a blank scope. All 5 changed/new files (public/app.php, config/navigation.json, config/kra-kpi.json, surface/KraKpi.php, the migration, and the test — 6 in total) copied to /mnt/user-data/outputs/, committed to the device at C:\laragon\www\SmartPRS3, then re-staged and byte-compared (cmp -s) against the outputs copies to confirm the write actually landed — all 6 matched exactly.
stopped_at: Code-complete and device-verified byte-exact. Not yet confirmed by the owner opening the two new screens live: publishing a scoped target, recording an achievement against it, and reading the % Achieved column back. The two tables ship as migrations but run on the file-store fallback until someone with terminal access runs them — expected and already true of most of this build.

title: KRAs and KPIs — a Keep checkbox per KPI, per scope, so KPI Achievements only ever offers what was actually kept for an employee's profile
detail: Owner's follow-up on the same day's KRA/KPI work: “Add a check box in the Organization Configuration tab to keep the particular KRAs/KPIs and only these should be reflected in the Performance tab for the respective profile logged in or selected.” Before this, a target box with a number was the only way a KPI applied to a scope at all — there was no way to say “this KPI matters for Pune collectors” before a number was agreed, and the KPI Achievements dropdown offered the entire 175-KPI catalogue to every employee regardless of what was actually configured for them. DID NOT ADD AN 'enabled' COLUMN: kept a KPI is — for an exact scope tuple — exactly a currently in-force row for it, number set or not, so target_value on kra_kpi_targets became nullable (safe: the migration has never run anywhere) rather than the catalogue growing a second, easily-out-of-sync flag. surface/KraKpi.php::publish() changed from a partial touch (only the codes named in the submitted map were closed/republished) to a FULL REPLACE of one exact scope tuple: it takes a new $keptCodes list, closes every row currently open for that tuple regardless of KPI, then republishes only the ticked codes — a target number if one was entered, null if the box was left blank. That is what makes unticking a KPI and re-saving actually remove it, rather than merely not touching it. Added a private winningRows() (asOf, company, branch, role) → kpi_code => winning row, using the exact 'skip only after an actual scope match' pattern ComponentRules::resolveFor() already uses for its $winners map — caught in review before it was ever committed: the first draft marked a code resolved the moment ANY row for it was seen, which would have wrongly stopped a less-specific row from being tried when the most-specific one didn't cover the employee. resolveTarget() now shares winningRows() and returns null both for 'nobody configured this' and for 'kept here, but no number yet' — a kept-but-numberless KPI still refuses record(), named accurately rather than as a silent zero. New public kpisEnabledFor(asOf, company, branch, role): the kept codes for a scope, array_keys(winningRows()) — the one list both the setup screen's prefill and the Achievements dropdown now agree on. public/app.php: kra-kpi-save reads a new keep[] checkbox array (hidden+'0' companion input, the same convention configure-menu already uses so an unticked box still submits) and passes it as $keptCodes; the KRAs and KPIs screen gained a Keep column — checkbox per KPI row, pre-checked from targetsForExactScope() — plus a 'keep all' / 'keep none' link per KRA (KPI codes share a stable kra-slug prefix before '--', confirmed with no exceptions across all 175, so one small script keys off it without a second per-KRA id anywhere). KPI Achievements was redesigned into a two-step, GET-based flow instead of a free-text-only form: ?emp=CODE resolves a profile, or (no code means your own — the same convention the 'me' self-service screen already uses via scope->own()) the signed-in account's own linked employee; scope->covers() gates seeing anyone else's, same as every other cross-employee read in this codebase. The KPI dropdown is filtered to kpisEnabledFor() for the resolved employee's own company/branch/role, grouped by KRA with empty KRA groups dropped, and the record form now posts the resolved employee's code as a hidden field instead of asking for it a second time — one lookup, not two employee inputs that could disagree. tests/kra_kpi_test.php rewritten for the new publish() signature plus new coverage: a kept-no-number KPI appears in kpisEnabledFor() but record() still refuses it; unticking a previously-kept KPI and re-saving removes it from kpisEnabledFor(); kpisEnabledFor() respects the same company/branch/role specificity precedence as resolveTarget() — 39 assertions, all passing.
found_wrong: The Request-1 shape conflated two separate facts into one column: 'this KPI counts for this scope' and 'here is the number for it'. Making target_value nullable and defining 'kept' as 'a row exists' (rather than adding a parallel enabled flag that could drift from the presence of a target row) keeps there being exactly one place that answers 'is this KPI live for this scope'.
got_wrong_first: First draft of kpisEnabledFor()'s scope-matching marked a KPI code as resolved the instant any row for that code was seen in targetsInForce(), not only on an actual scope match — which would have wrongly given up on a code the moment its most-specific row failed to cover the employee, instead of falling through to try a less-specific row for the same code. Caught in review before any file was written; fixed by only setting $winners[$code] inside the branch that confirms a match, mirroring ComponentRules::resolveFor() exactly.

title: KRAs and KPIs — fixed the target/achievement redundancy in the 175-KPI catalogue (role system)
detail:
Owner reviewed the KRAs and KPIs screen (Field Collection KRA, 12 KPIs) and flagged it as “not logically correct”: a genuine planned figure (Field Visits Assigned), the matching actual figure (Field Visits Completed) and the ratio between them (Visit Completion %) were all sitting side by side as independent, keepable, targetable rows in Organization Configuration — when only the planned figure belongs there, the actual figure belongs in Performance & Rewards → KPI Achievements recorded against that target, and the ratio is something the system already computes and should never be a separate stored/targeted number (Law 4 — every number explains itself — plus it invites drift between the stored ratio and the real target/achievement pair). Asked to check the entire 175-KPI catalogue for the same pattern and correct it everywhere it occurs, not just the one named example.

Added a role system to the catalogue rather than deleting rows: each KPI optionally carries role=target|achievement|computed plus, for achievement/computed, measures_against naming the target KPI's code. No role (the default — 164 of 175 rows) means 'standalone', the original universal behaviour (targetable in Org Config AND achievable against itself in Performance) — nothing changes for those. Detection was deliberately mechanical, not judgment-based: a script parsed every ratio-shaped formula (A ÷ B × 100) and matched its two operand phrases against sibling KPI names in the SAME KRA by full token overlap. Only 4 KRAs produced a clean 2/2 match on both operands — Collection & Recovery, Field Collection, and two pairs inside Agent Productivity (accounts worked, accounts resolved, both against accounts assigned) — giving 11 rows reclassified in total:
  field-collection--field-visits-assigned → role: target
  field-collection--field-visits-completed → role: achievement, measures_against: field-visits-assigned
  field-collection--visit-completion → role: computed, measures_against: field-visits-assigned (no longer targetable or recordable on its own — % Achieved in Performance already is this number)
  collection-recovery--collection-target → role: target
  collection-recovery--collection-amount → role: achievement, measures_against: collection-target
  collection-recovery--collection-achievement → role: computed, measures_against: collection-target
  agent-productivity--accounts-assigned → role: target
  agent-productivity--accounts-worked → role: achievement, measures_against: accounts-assigned
  agent-productivity--account-coverage → role: computed, measures_against: accounts-assigned
  agent-productivity--accounts-resolved → role: achievement, measures_against: accounts-assigned
  agent-productivity--resolution-productivity → role: computed, measures_against: accounts-assigned
The remaining ~164 rows (Delinquency Management, Bucket Management, Compliance, Data Quality, SLA/TAT and most others) are almost entirely pure ratio/rate KPIs with no raw count pair anywhere in the matrix to split them against — left untouched as standalone rather than guessed at. This is a narrower cut than the owner's 'check for all similar' instruction taken at face value; flagged explicitly back to them so they can name any other KRA where they know the specific target/achievement pairing and want the same split.

surface/KraKpi.php: added ROLE_TARGET/ROLE_ACHIEVEMENT/ROLE_COMPUTED constants; byKra() kept as the raw grouping and reused via a new groupedByKra(Closure $keep) helper; added configurableByKra() (excludes achievement+computed — for Organization Configuration) and achievableByKra() (excludes target+computed — for KPI Achievements); added roleOf(), targetKpiFor() (resolves an achievement/computed code to the target code it measures_against, or itself if standalone) and achievementsMeasuring($targetCode) (for the 'measured by' UI hint). publish() now refuses to keep an achievement or computed code directly, with a message naming why. resolveTarget() and kpisEnabledFor() now resolve through targetKpiFor() so an achievement KPI is enabled/targeted via its paired target row, not its own (nonexistent) target row. record()'s refusal messages now name the actual target KPI when recording against a different code than the target.

public/app.php: Organization Configuration now calls configurableByKra() and shows a badge-blue 'measured by' hint under any target KPI that has achievements recorded against it elsewhere, linking the two screens visually; KPI Achievements now calls achievableByKra() and its KPI dropdown shows '(target: <name>)' next to any achievement-role KPI. The 'why this is a choice' panel gained a paragraph explaining the three roles and the badge.

tests/kra_kpi_test.php: switched the generic/standalone test KPI from collection-recovery--collection-amount (now role=achievement) to customer-service--customer-complaints, with an explicit assertion that it carries no role. Added a full 'ROLES' section covering the Field Collection triplet end to end: role and measures_against assertions on all three codes; configurableByKra()/achievableByKra() filtering; publish() refusing the achievement and computed codes directly with the right reasons; record() refusing before the target is published and naming Field Visits Assigned in the refusal; then publish target=200 (scoped to Chennai), confirm kpisEnabledFor() now includes the achievement code, record 180 and confirm target_value=200 and percent_achieved=90.
checks: php -l clean on config/kra-kpi.json (validated as JSON via python json.load), surface/KraKpi.php and public/app.php. tests/kra_kpi_test.php rewritten and run: 59 assertions, 0 failures (up from 39 — 20 new ROLES assertions, all passing on the first run once the target/achievement/computed wiring was in). Full suite (php tests/run.php): 61 assertions, 2 failures — both pre-existing and unrelated (component_rules_test: config/salary-components.json missing in this sandbox; pay_cycles_test: Customisation class unresolvable in this sandbox) — kra_kpi itself is clean. All four changed files (config/kra-kpi.json, surface/KraKpi.php, public/app.php, tests/kra_kpi_test.php) committed to C:\laragon\www\SmartPRS3 and re-staged + byte-compared (cmp -s) against the committed copies — all four matched byte-exact on the FIRST commit attempt this time (no repeat of the earlier silent-write-failure pattern, but the verification step was still run in full per standing policy on this project).

title: Codebase-wide nav/route/module mismatch audit — 49 real screens unhidden, compliance/compliance-alerts split corrected, Screen Guide continued
detail:
Owner asked, after the Salary Advance/Loans regression was fixed: “ensure this is fixed properly at all the places and no mismatch again for any modules”, plus to continue the Screen Guide for the remaining pending modules including Salary Advance and Loans. The regression's root cause — checking public/app.php for a literal $route === '<name>' and missing the generic surface/screens/<route>.php catch-all dispatch (line ~8402, self-documented in the app's own menu-customisation validator at ~5089-5119) — turned out to have produced several other wrong 'dead route'/'not built' conclusions earlier the same day, in the Statutory & Compliance Screen Guide pass specifically.

Replicated the app's own answered-routes computation in a script instead of checking route-by-route: union of every literal $route==='x' match, every in_array($route,[...],true) block, every real surface/screens/*.php filename (taken from the device listing directly, 63 files — a first draft under-counted because only 2 files happened to be staged locally), and the $setupScreens keys. Diffed that set against every config/navigation.d/*.json item's route/module reference, and separately grepped the whole app for r=<route> occurrences to tell 'hidden but reachable via a contextual link' apart from 'hidden with zero inbound link anywhere' (the actual bug).

Result: zero genuinely dead routes anywhere in the app. 49 nav items across admin, extras (time/admin/payroll), field-reports, letters-comm, leave-comp, time, perf-learn and statutory sections were hidden (or, for two items, pointed at the wrong route) despite being backed by real, complete, zero-inbound-link-elsewhere screens — same pattern as Salary Advance/Loans, at much larger scale. 7 nav items referenced a "module" key absent from config/modules.json.

Also found: the earlier same-day fix that repointed 'compliance-alerts' at route 'compliance' had itself conflated two real, different screens — Compliance Watch (per-person DRA/PCC/bank-authorisation/document expiry, route 'compliance') and Compliance Alerts (per-obligation statutory filing due-dates from config/compliance-calendar.json, route 'compliance-alerts', its own screen entirely) — which cross-link to each other in the real code. Reverted and split back into two correct nav items.
found: 49 real-but-hidden screens (listed in claude/changes_2026-09-16_nav-mismatch-audit.md, a project doc); the compliance/compliance-alerts conflation described above; greetings and greetings-log both pointed at a non-existent 'greetings' module despite surface/screens/greetings.php being real and already combining both; sms-templates nav item pointed at a non-existent module despite the sms_templates table already existing (shared with the real wa-templates module); smtp-settings and the two 'overtime' nav items pointed at modules with genuinely no backing table anywhere — confirmed via a full grep of database/migrations, not assumed.
what_i_got_wrong_first: The five Statutory & Compliance 'not built' Screen Guide entries written earlier the same day (gratuity, tds, statutory-bonus, audit-reports, statutory-config) were themselves wrong for the identical missed-dispatch-mechanism reason as the Salary Advance regression — all five are real, complete screens. The gratuity entry in particular had been marked 'fabricated' when in fact the real screen implements almost exactly what was described. Corrected in full in claude/changes_2026-09-16_statutory-guide.md.

title: Learning & Knowledge real content — the missing seeder found and ported
detail: User showed smartprs.com/app (live) with 12 real Training Programs and 24 real Training Content rows, vs 0 on this local build, and asked directly why real content documented as ported earlier (see the 2026-09-16 learning-helpdesk doc) wasn't actually there. Re-investigated and found the earlier 'SmartPRS2 has no real seed content' conclusion was wrong: it only grepped app/Http/Controllers/*.php for a defaults()-style method, and never looked in app/Console/Commands/. SmartPRS2 has a dedicated 80KB Artisan command there, SeedIndustryContent.php (php artisan content:seed-industry), that inserts detailed India-compliant Collections & Recovery industry content into training_programs, training_subjects, faqs and kb_topics for every tenant plus the global KB. Ported its actual data (not the command itself, since this install runs on the JSON file store, not SQL) into storage/training_programs.json (+12), storage/training_content.json (+24), storage/faqs.json (+17), storage/kb_topics.json (+15), and added a missing 'description' field to the training-programs module in config/modules.json (SmartPRS2 had added that column ad hoc; this repo never had it).

Root cause: app.php's sidebar accordion (~line 6804) auto-opens only the section whose item route matches the current route exactly; a hand-maintained $orphanRouteSection map (~line 6460, added earlier this session) is the escape hatch for drill-down screens with no nav item of their own, but it only covered 9 routes. title: Working Shifts also collapsed the sidebar -- a second, different bug in the same mechanism
detail: User reported the sidebar collapsing again, this time on Working Shifts under Organization Setup/Configuration -- but that item has its own declared nav route (setup-shifts), so it's not a drill-down orphan like the last fix. title: "Incomplete guide" report -- fixed a real scroll-reset bug plus 5 genuine content gaps across all 157 Screen Guide entries
detail: User reported the Leave & Absence Screen Guide as incomplete, with a screenshot showing text starting mid-sentence. Read the actual leave-absence entry in full: every field was present and matched the screenshot exactly -- the content was never missing. Root cause was in the dialog's own JS: .help-body never resets scrollTop on reopen (showModal()) or on tab switch (helpTab()), and since the <dialog> persists in the DOM, reopening the guide keeps whatever scroll position was left, making a complete guide look like it starts mid-thought. title: Leave & Absence: real Abscond/Unauthorized-Absence documentation, plus Leave Type eligibility (Company/Branch/Role/Designation, Marital Status for ML/PL)
detail: Two-part ask from the owner. Part A: 'nothing mentioned about Abscond or Unauthorized Absence' in the Screen Guide -- read the actual UnauthorizedAbsence.php/config/unauthorized-absence.json behaviour (run-based escalation, not day-based; a weekly-off or holiday inside a run neither counts toward it nor breaks it; a real punch or approved leave ends it outright; four configurable day-thresholds -- Abscond, First Warning, Second Warning, Final FnF; always_cc_designations with Company Admin/Branch Admin/HR Admin/HR Manager shipped defaults, preferring a holder in the employee's own company; manual Evaluate/Run) and rewrote the leave-absence screen-help.json entry's f/s/tip/why/uc/adv to actually describe it, instead of one vague bullet. Part B: eligibility columns for Leave Types (Company/Branch/Role/Designation dropdowns after Note) plus Maternity/Paternity restricted to Married employees. Investigation found this was NOT a build-from-scratch: SmartPRS\Surface\LeavePolicy already had a marital-status mechanism (hidden_for_marital_status, used by LeavePolicy::typesFor()) from an earlier pass, but (1) ML/PL only hid the type for 'Single', which is not the same as 'only Married' -- Divorced and Widowed were still shown -- and (2) it was cosmetic: only used in 3 balance-display call sites, never checked when a leave request or grant was actually made. Fixed the data (hidden_for_marital_status now lists Single/Divorced/Widowed for both ML and PL, so 'hidden for everyone who isn't Married' actually reads as 'only Married'). Added the real feature: LeavePolicy::SCOPE_DIMENSIONS (company/branch/role/designation) plus eligible()/ineligibleReason(), reusing Leave Grants' own 'every named scope must match, blank matches everybody' convention and the ID Card Format screen's existing pattern for resolving free-text Role from a designation. typesFor() now takes the whole employment context, not just marital status. Wired ELIGIBILITY, not just display: the leave-request POST handler now refuses (with a plain-English reason) before Leave::request() is even called if the type doesn't apply to the requesting employee; LeaveGrants::reach() takes an optional LeavePolicy and excludes any employee the grant's own scope reaches but the TYPE itself does not allow -- this is the one that actually matters for ML/PL today, since the product's self-service leave-request form is presently hardcoded to EL only (a pre-existing, separate limitation, left alone -- not something this ask reported) and Maternity/Paternity are realistically HR-administered via Grants. Added the Company/Branch/Role/Designation columns to the Leave Types table itself, saved through LeavePolicy::saveTypes() exactly like every other column. Verified with two standalone PHP self-checks (16 assertions on LeavePolicy::eligible()/typesFor(), 2 on LeaveGrants::reach()'s backward-compatible optional policy argument) before touching the device.
found: surface/LeavePolicy.php already had typesFor(?string $maritalStatus) and hidden_for_marital_status wired to 3 display call sites in app.php -- a real, working mechanism, just incomplete and cosmetic-only
ML/PL's hidden_for_marital_status was ['Single'] only -- Divorced and Widowed employees were incorrectly still shown/granted these types
config/employee-fields.json already declares marital_status as a real employees column (List: Single/Married/Divorced/Widowed) -- no schema change needed

The self-service leave-request form (route=leave) hardcodes leave_type=EL -- there is currently no UI path for an employee to self-request ML/PL/CO/etc at all; the realistic path for ML/PL is HR granting it via Leave Grants

LeaveGrants already has a full, generic 'any named scope must match, blank matches everybody' mechanism (company/branch/department/designation/team/employee) -- reused its convention rather than inventing a second one

The ID Card Format screen already resolves a free-text 'Role' (Role/Designation Setup, not employees.role the access tier) via orgValueOf($store, $e, 'role') keyed off designation_id -- reused that exact resolution for the new Role eligibility dimension

The picker is also deliberately short: $exWithout excludes any employee who already has an exits row, since Settlement::quote() already refuses a second settlement for the same employment. (2): Settlement::quote()/settle() gained $otherEarnings/$otherDeductions parameters, each line validated by a new private parseOtherLines() against ComponentRules::components() (config/salary-components.json) so every line names a component already declared in Salary Structure and matches the kind (earning/deduction) it is posted as -- never a free-text label typed at settlement time (Law 1). The settlement screen (route=settlement) gained two GET 'Add earning' / 'Add deduction' mini-forms (pick a configured component, type an amount and a required note, same 'compute, read, then record' GET-quote/POST-record shape the screen already used for last working day) plus Remove links, all carried into the POST 'Record this settlement' form as hidden inputs so what was quoted is exactly what gets recorded. Writing a settlement's lines into it as a fabricated single-employee run would be read by verify() as a run that cannot be reproduced, and could double-count in whatever reads $register->runs() (bank advice export, PF/ESI and other statutory reports) -- so this pass does NOT do that. title: Dev console guard: widen localhost-only to private-LAN (public/index.php)
detail: Owner ran `php -S 0.0.0.0:8001 -t public` (to reach the console from another machine on the office network) and hit `public/index.php`'s hardcoded 403 -- REMOTE_ADDR was the requesting LAN machine's address (192.168.0.141), not 127.0.0.1/::1, so the existing `in_array($remote, ['127.0.0.1','::1',''])` guard (the comment above it: "a dev console over an unauthenticated database... the cheapest closed door is the only one that exists until identity is wired in") tripped as designed. Asked the owner how far to widen it rather than guessing, given Law 5 (fails closed): offered allow-the-whole-private-LAN, allow-one-specific-IP, or remove-the-guard. Owner chose the private-LAN option. Replaced the flat allowlist with $isLocalhost (unchanged: 127.0.0.1/::1/empty) OR $isPrivateLan (valid IP AND filter_var($remote, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE) === false, i.e. it IS in an RFC1918/private range) -- still exits 403 for any public IP. Updated the exit message from 'localhost-only' to 'local-network-only' since that's no longer accurate otherwise. Only public/index.php had this guard; public/app.php and public/api.php do not duplicate it, so they were left untouched.
found: PHP's FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE only excludes IPv4 RFC1918 ranges and the IPv6 unique-local range (fc00::/7); IPv6 link-local (fe80::/10) falls under FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE instead and is NOT covered by this check, so a same-subnet peer reached only via an IPv6 link-local address would still be blocked. Not handled -- out of scope for the LAN-IPv4 case actually reported, flagged here rather than silently left undocumented.
checks: php -l clean on public/index.php. Standalone fixture (no server, no DB): reimplemented the guard's exact expression in a php -r one-liner and ran it against 12 addresses (127.0.0.1, ::1, empty, three private IPv4s across all three RFC1918 blocks, a just-outside-172.16/12 address, two public IPv4s, a public IPv6, and the fe80::1 edge case above) -- 11/12 as expected, the fe80::1 case behaving per the 'found' note above, not a defect in the intended IPv4-LAN fix. NOT run: composer check/gates/pest -- no shell on the linked computer this session, only file staging; owner should reload the console from the other machine to confirm and run `composer check` on the Laragon machine.
stopped_at: public/index.php's guard widened and verified standalone; not yet confirmed against a live request from the other machine, and composer check has not been run.

detail: Owner: (4) Admin/HR Manager/anyone a team reports to should see regularization requests from their whole hierarchy — direct reports, team members, and teams under their team leads; (5) every employee, Admin included, can apply; Company Admin self-approves. title: Appearance: a theme picker in the topbar, light and dark, seven presets
detail: Owner asked for a theme button top right, several themes with a preview, light/dark, and some customisation. Two independent attributes on <html>: data-mode (light|dark, resolved from the OS when the choice is 'System') and data-theme (a preset). A preset sets SIX variables only — the accent trio and the navy trio — so each one works in light and in dark without a second definition. Also data-density (table row padding) and data-scale (zoom on .content, for the standing 'too small on a small screen' complaint), and an optional custom accent written inline on <html>. Kept in localStorage and read by a script at the top of <head>, before the first paint: every click here is a full page load, so a preference applied late is a white flash on every navigation. PRECEDENCE, by design: custom accent > chosen preset > the company's App Branding colour > the stock orange. The first preset card carries an EMPTY key — it clears the attribute and lets App Branding show through — so the administrator's colour stays the default everybody starts on and a personal pick is an override of it. No new action handler, no config file, no table: the choice is per person, per browser.
found: Six accent gradients (.topbar-avatar, .login-logo, .profile-avatar, .ai-ava, .payslip-logo .ico, .bubble.user) faded var(--accent) into a LITERAL #ea580c, so under any theme but orange they ran e.g. indigo-to-orange. Now fade into var(--accent2). This was wrong in light mode too, and is the only pixel that changed there.
input[type=checkbox]/[type=radio] hardcoded accent-color:#f97316 — now var(--accent).
.topbar-btn is a literal #fff; left unanswered it rendered three white tiles in a dark header. Caught on the first render, not by reading the file.
got_wrong_first: Declared the dark .card-header h3 rule BEFORE .card h3. They match at equal specificity and the light sheet settles the tie by source order, so every card title came out accent-orange instead of text-coloured. Moved after. Also wrote the preset/dark selectors as bare attribute selectors first — same specificity as :root, and the branding <style> that writes :root is emitted AFTER the stylesheet, so it won and every preset still showed the company colour. Prefixed html[...] to outrank it.
checks: Both stylesheets and the inline <style> block parse with zero errors (tinycss2). php -l clean. Rendered in Chromium: light/dark x 8 presets, the picker, density and scale, no page errors.
